construct: A ventral midbrain lesion can injure exiting oculomotor nerve fascicles together with descending corticospinal and corticobulbar fibers in the cerebral peduncle. This produces an ipsilateral third-nerve palsy with contralateral weakness.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Ipsilateral complete CN III palsy with contralateral pure motor weakness and no prominent ataxia localizes to the ventral midbrain where oculomotor fascicles traverse the cerebral peduncle.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Oculomotor fascicle plus red nucleus injury can cause a crossed midbrain syndrome, but red-nucleus involvement predicts contralateral tremor/ataxia rather than the predominantly pyramidal deficit described.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The motor phenotype and absence of cerebellar signs make CN III fascicle plus cerebral peduncle the unique localization.
